items.text: Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune as their leader by secret ballot; he ran unopposed and will lead them in the minority from January. Sen. Ron Johnson, who had sought a delay, walked out as voting began.

Trump said the US has already won the Iran war and now wants “total victory”. At the G7 in Paris, Rubio said the US is not on a path to restart a hot war and will keep squeezing Iran’s economy rather than accept a “stupid deal” (per Axios, cited by Fox). Iran threatened to strike US bases in Europe if they are used to attack it.
items.notes: Closes W-261106-03. Iran Europe-bases threat from Times of Israel live-blog headline only.

items.text: Treasury Secretary Bessent has moved from his Washington home to a military base after Iranian threats against his life, the New York Times reported; a senior official told Fox the plotting had reached an advanced stage, and Rubio and Stephen Miller have also moved to protected housing. Iran has previously denied plotting attacks on US soil.
An oil tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran’s IRGC (via AP); UKMTO reported a tanker incident but it is unclear whether it is the same ship.

Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, possibly within days, the Wall Street Journal reported, after the New York Times reported a second alleged affair, with a senior Nvidia executive. No decision had been confirmed. Shares rose nearly 5% in regular trading, then fell about 7.5% after hours; House Republicans are threatening to subpoena Huang.
items.outlet: ABC7 / San Francisco Standard (citing WSJ, NYT)

items.text: Reuters found procurement records showing an Entity-Listed Chinese military university bought Nvidia H200 chips through a reseller without a licence, and flagged 26 similar records. Senators Warren and Coons asked the administration to preserve records on H200 export licensing to China.
items.notes: Read via AI Weekly summary; original Reuters/Al Jazeera pages not reachable.

items.text: With about a month to the government funding deadline, Congress is far from a spending deal, the Washington Post reported; Bloomberg reported Democrats are weighing using funding to press for an end to the Iran war.
items.notes: Headlines only; full articles not reachable.

items.text: CISA added a critical (CVSS 9.8) GPUStack authentication flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue, with a Nov 12 deadline for federal agencies to fix it.

Warsaw city hall estimated up to 250,000 people at the nationalist Independence March (organisers claimed at least twice that, against about 100,000 last year by the city’s count). It was largely peaceful, but flares were lit despite a ban, three marchers burned a Lewica flag on Poniatowski Bridge, and police detained 60 people, mostly for drug possession. President Nawrocki had announced he would take part.
items.notes: Closes W-261106-08. Detention figure from TVN24. Nawrocki attendance from his pre-march announcement (OKO.press); not confirmed in sources read.

items.text: In his Independence Day speech on Piłsudski Square, Nawrocki said the Constitutional Tribunal’s prestige had been “buried” in recent weeks, warned against elites looking to Berlin and Moscow, and told Finance Minister Domański to do better on public finances. Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz, partly booed, defended Domański and said trust in the Tribunal was lost years ago.

Tusk, speaking in Szczecin, invited Nawrocki and his family to a pre-Christmas gathering at his home in Sopot so they could talk. Nawrocki did not respond; his chief of staff Bogucki mocked Tusk on X as a “dove of peace”. The Domański, Bartol and NBP board appointments remain unsigned.

PiS leader Kaczyński told Onet his party will work toward “one big list” of the right for both the Sejm and the Senate at next year’s election; Konfederacja’s Mentzen answered with a pointed photo on X.

Orlen gave notice terminating its 2009 oil-indexed contract with QatarEnergy for 1 million tonnes of LNG a year (due to run to 2034), citing QatarEnergy’s ongoing force majeure since Iranian strikes on Qatari plants. The deal ends 60 days after notice. Orlen says gas supply security is not affected; it keeps a second Qatari contract and US LNG deals. It is the first QatarEnergy buyer to cancel.
items.notes: Termination confirmed by Orlen regulatory filing (per Bloomberg, The National).

items.text: Digital Affairs Minister Gawkowski said a cyberattack on ePUAP, the state e-government platform, was detected and stopped on Tuesday evening; the platform was taken offline as a precaution and was still down on Wednesday with no restoration date. The ministry says the system was not compromised and the ABW is investigating. No data leak has been reported.

The European Commission published an implementing regulation, (EU) 2026/2487, setting common rules for national AI regulatory sandboxes under the AI Act, which Poland, like other member states, must run.
items.notes: EU decision applying in Poland. Primary text on EUR-Lex not checked.

items.text: At Kraków’s Independence Day ceremonies, Małopolska voivode Klęczar said that “as Poland in 1918, Kraków today returns to life”, refusing to name the gunman and calling him a killer “without a human face”.

Senior constable Artur Morański, 27, wounded in the right hand while detaining the Main Square gunman, had another operation (wound revision and elbow fusion); his doctor says he has a chance of regaining use of the hand.

The Union Cabinet extended the Stand-Up India scheme for women, SC and ST entrepreneurs to March 2031 with a ₹4,111 crore credit guarantee corpus, aiming at 2.5 lakh more borrowers (loans of ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore). It also extended the micro-loan guarantee fund (CGFMU) to 2031 with ₹5,000 crore and cut the Mudra guarantee fee from 1% to 0.75%.

The Cabinet approved nutrient-based subsidy rates for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for the 2026-27 rabi season; the reported cost is about ₹62,370 crore, up from ₹37,952 crore last rabi, as global prices stay high.
items.notes: Figure not yet matched to PIB release.

items.text: The DGFT moved lithium-ion battery “black mass” (recycling feedstock) from free to prohibited for export (Notification 49/2026-27) to keep it for domestic recyclers.
The production-linked incentive scheme for medical devices was extended to 2035-36 with about ₹2,700 crore, dropping the minimum sales threshold and lowering the minimum investment.
Indian stocks rallied: the Sensex rose 772.75 points to 81,879.40 and the Nifty 50 rose 210.40 to 25,255.05; the rupee closed at 93.69 to the dollar.
The Defence Ministry signed a ₹498.58 crore contract with Cochin Shipyard to refit the frigate INS Betwa, switching it from steam to diesel propulsion.
The cabinet economic committee approved ₹3,230 crore for the Yuge Yugeen Bharat national museum in Delhi’s North and South Blocks; the first gallery is expected in late 2027.
